## Reasoning

**Step 1: Tensile strength from the table**

For W fibers (50 vol%) in copper (parallel loading of continuous filaments):
$$\text{T.S.} = 1100 \text{ MPa}$$

**Step 2: Composite density (rule of mixtures)**

Using standard densities $\rho_W = 19.3$ g/cm³ and $\rho_{Cu} = 8.9$ g/cm³:
$$\rho_c = V_W\rho_W + V_{Cu}\rho_{Cu} = 0.5(19.3) + 0.5(8.9) = 14.1 \text{ g/cm}^3 = 14100 \text{ kg/m}^3$$

**Step 3: Specific strength (breaking length)**

Specific strength as a length (the only interpretation consistent with a length unit of mm) is the breaking length:
$$L = \frac{\sigma}{\rho g} = \frac{1100\times10^6 \text{ Pa}}{(14100 \text{ kg/m}^3)(9.8 \text{ m/s}^2)} \approx 7961 \text{ m}$$

Converting to mm:
$$L \approx 7961 \times 10^3 \text{ mm} \approx 7.96\times10^6 \text{ mm}$$

This is physically sensible — a breaking length of ~8 km for a strong tungsten‑reinforced copper composite.

$$\boxed{7.96\times10^{6}}$$
